title: analytics: a cross-object leaf in a dataset measure's own filter served as the engine's semi-join (aggregations[].filter)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1QwJJ5KGZTThP4fnq

Follow-up of #33626 (draft PR #33652). ⛔ Not a claim.

## What exists

#33626 asks that the dataset's own `filter` and its per-measure filters compile through the same semi-join. PR #33652 serves the dataset's own definition-level `filter` (and a `where` leaf up to three relationships) on the analytics engine-aggregate path. A cross-object leaf in ONE MEASURE's own `filter` (`measures[].filter: { 'account.region': 'West' }`) is still refused `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 by `ObjectQLStrategy.planCrossObject`, and the engine itself refuses the nested form at `aggregations[N].filter` (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400, "which the engine serves in 'where'").

## Why it did not fit #33652

The engine composes `ReadableIds` leaves only on `where` at its executor boundary (ADR-0139 D2). A per-aggregation `filter` is a conditional aggregate the driver compiles (or the engine evaluates over rows it holds); serving a semi-join there needs the boundary to compose leaves inside each `aggregations[].filter`, driver-sql to compile the subquery inside the conditional aggregate, and the in-memory bucketing path (non-UTC timezone) to evaluate it.

## What lands

The engine serves the nested-relation condition at `aggregations[N].filter` on read verbs (planned related read, composed leaf, same read scope per hop); analytics respells a measure filter's dotted leaf as it now respells the dataset `filter`; both SQL-echo faces refuse in the where-door envelope. Tests: parity with the `where` route per measure, the related row scope under `$ne`.

## Grade

p2.
